close_reason:
Fixed in f91f908. Added a demotion-detection pass that runs after the regular create+update+destroy loops in handle_address_book_set. Captures the set of currently-default AddressBook ids ONCE at the top, then re-fetches after the loops and inserts any flipped-to-false entries into the wire 'updated' map. Skips ids that already have authoritative records in 'updated' or 'created'.

Pass runs BEFORE the existing onSuccessSetIsDefault block to avoid double-attribution. The pre-existing over-inclusion bug in the onSuccessSetIsDefault block (it inserts books that were never default at the start) is NOT touched here — out of scope; can be folded into the same machinery later if needed.

Three new integration tests on MemoryBackend exercise:
- update-with-isDefault: demoted sibling appears in wire updated
- create-with-isDefault: demoted sibling appears in wire updated
- regular update without isDefault: 'updated' is NOT polluted with unrelated sibling entries (regression guard)

94+36+1 contacts-server tests pass; workspace clippy + tests + doc clean.
description:
## Context

The MemoryBackend (and any conformant backend) now atomically demotes other AddressBooks when an update OR create makes one default (bd:JMAP-qz9v.5 and bd:JMAP-qz9v.11). The wire 'updated' map in AddressBook/set response only reflects the change for the directly-targeted book; demoted siblings are NOT surfaced.

The onSuccessSetIsDefault block at addressbook.rs:413-440 DOES re-fetch all other books after a successful patch and inserts demoted ones into 'updated'. The regular update path at addressbook.rs:248-281 does NOT. The create path at addressbook.rs:194-223 does NOT.

## Wire consequence

A client that does:
  AddressBook/set { create: { c1: { isDefault: true, ... } } }
or:
  AddressBook/set { update: { ab1: { isDefault: true } } }

…gets a response that ONLY mentions the created/promoted book in 'updated' even though one or more sibling books were just server-demoted to isDefault:false. The client's local cache then thinks both books are still default, in violation of RFC 9610 §2 'MUST NOT be true for more than one'.

The /changes machinery does report the demotion (the backend records demoted ids in the change_log per bd:JMAP-qz9v.5/.11), but that requires the client to follow up with AddressBook/changes. RFC 8620 §5.3 expects the /set response itself to carry all changes for objects that were modified beyond the client's explicit request.

## Approach options

(a) Handler re-fetches all AddressBooks after each successful create-with-isDefault or update-with-isDefault and inserts demoted ones into 'updated'. Mirrors the onSuccessSetIsDefault pattern at addressbook.rs:422-440.

(b) Backend trait returns Vec<Id> of demoted books alongside the created/updated object. Handler converts the list to /get calls or maintains its own demoted-set. Cleaner backend->handler contract but requires trait change.

(c) Document the gap as a workspace-policy choice ('the server may signal side-effect changes via /changes only; clients SHOULD follow /set with /changes').

Recommendation: (a) — matches existing onSuccessSetIsDefault pattern, no trait change, localized fix in the handler.

## Scope

- Update create branch in handle_address_book_set to re-fetch siblings after a successful create that set isDefault:true; insert demoted entries into 'updated'.
- Update update branch similarly.
- Two integration tests on MemoryBackend exercising the wire 'updated' map contains demoted books for both paths.

## Related

- bd:JMAP-qz9v.5 (closed, MemoryBackend create-side invariant landed)
- bd:JMAP-qz9v.11 (closed, MemoryBackend update-side invariant landed)
- onSuccessSetIsDefault path already covers the test in src/addressbook.rs::set_on_success_reports_demoted_book_in_updated
title: Handler: report demoted AddressBooks in wire 'updated' on regular create+update paths
